lines.required_change: exactRegion builds ONE arrangement of all the original segments — the rings and every part — at once: every intersection of two ORIGINAL segments found with exact predicates (orient2d), the point an exact rational N/D in BigInt; the cells classed by winding (inside the rings, inside no part: the parts' windings summed, so a ring set with holes may stand as one part, line 10); the boundary traced. THE ROUNDING RULE, stated in kerbExact.ts's header and proved by the pins: every output vertex is an input vertex or the ONE half-away-from-zero rounding of the exact intersection of two original segments — computed WITHOUT DIVISION: a double estimate (through ratio()) corrected by BigInt multiply-compares until (2k − 1)·|D| ≤ 2·|N| < (2k + 1)·|D| holds for the sign-adjusted k, then snap's range check — never a rounding of a point computed from a rounded point. Where that rounding would leave a ring non-simple, the seat states its resolution and shows it order-free (e.g. one pass of snap rounding over the whole arrangement: every original segment routed through the centre of every hot pixel of a rounded vertex it passes — the hot pixels being every vertex of exactRegion's own input (the rings and parts it is given) and every rounded intersection — so a ring vertex the key dropped, absent from that input, makes none, line 1 (7)). Hence X does not depend on the order of the spines, of their parts, of a ring's start or of the holes. PINS (derived.test.ts): (a) THE ORDER PROPERTY — fast-check over line 9's faces and over random part sets on random rings: exactRegion of every permutation drawn (spines and parts shuffled, ring starts rotated, holes reversed) byte-identical; (b) every output vertex a lattice point, and either an input vertex or the half-away rounding of an exact intersection of two input segments (the test recomputes the candidates in BigInt and asserts membership); (c) every output ring simpleRing (line 2's exemption apart), nesting as a region's rings do (nestingProblems); (d) the rounding's own pins at exact halves of both signs (+x.5 → up, −x.5 → down) and next to them (x.5 ± 1⁄D). DRAWS ARE FILTERED, NEVER MASSAGED: a network is discarded — and COUNTED — where a chord's route, walked by the test along the edges carrying its own row, leaves the line through its placed points by more than HOT_PIXEL_CM; lane landings are drawn more than attractCm (LATTICE.attractCm) from every vertex of F's boundary, so planCut splits an edge and never lands on a vertex, and a cut whose children's rings do not hold the lane's placed points exactly is discarded and counted; the kept share has its floor in line 9. F's spines: the chains whose placed route carries a route edge of F within HOT_PIXEL_CM (edge spines), or passes a route vertex of F only (vertex-only, kept where its buffer covers a sample in no edge spine's buffer). A buffer is the exact set {q : dist(q, route) ≤ hw}, round joins, ends as declared or flat — no chords, no snap. THE JUDGEMENT, TWO-SIDED: (1) a 20 cm grid over F: every sample farther than the MARGIN from every boundary (F's rings, each buffer's boundary, X's rings) lies in X exactly when it lies in no spine's buffer; (2) no vertex of X deeper than the margin in any spine's buffer, and every vertex of X within the margin of F's boundary or of a buffer's boundary; (3) every ring of X simpleRing (line 2's exemption apart). THE MARGIN, with its full sum (S18R-13): at an arc, SAGITTA_CM 2 + a part point's snap √2⁄2 + the intersection's rounding √2⁄2 = 3.41 cm; on a straight strip, the straight-through drop 2 · HOT_PIXEL_CM (1.42) + √2⁄2 + √2⁄2 = 2.84 cm; taken as 4 cm. THE ORACLE'S OWN PINS: it passes line 8's literal rings; it fails, by name, a planted X with one spine left out, one with a band at half its width, one shifted 10 cm. MUTANTS of X killed by it on line 9's corpus: OM1 one spine skipped; OM2 a band at half its width; OM3 the winding reversed.
